_comment: A CONSTRUCTED response, not a captured one -- no live call was made to produce it. It is shaped exactly like what messages.parse returns for the motor_housing project plus the committed CAD targets, and it exists so the validation in propose_ai.py can be tested without a network or an API key. Each candidate after the first two is a way a well-formed answer can still be fiction: an invented CAD object, an attribute the part does not have, bbox_size with no axis, and a measurement the target does not offer. If you replace this with a genuine recorded response, keep those cases -- they are the ones worth testing.

candidates.rationale: The script declares LENGTH_MM, and the part name matches the module name; bounding box along X, which is not necessarily a named feature dimension.
The module declares MATERIAL AlSi10Mg with a density, so mass follows from the geometry without an override.
A revised housing export would be the better source for the as-designed length.
A housing normally has a wall thickness and the script has a Z extent.
The gearbox housing is a plausible alternative source for the length.
Mass of the housing node in the assembly export.
